\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حديثا} (ḥadīthan)}{حديثا (ḥadīthan)}]{\ar{حديثا} (ḥadīthan) — recently}

\label{lesson:AR-C156-hadithan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for hot, then the Arabic for crowded.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حديثا}}
\textbf{\ar{حديثا}} — \emph{ḥadīthan} — \textquotedblleft{}recently\textquotedblright{}. Arabic's past for \textquotedblleft{}I\textquotedblright{} ends in \textbf{-\ar{تُ}} (\emph{-tu}): \textbf{\ar{قرأت} \ar{حديثا} \ar{كتابا} \ar{جميلا}} — \emph{qaraʾtu ḥadīthan kitāban jamīlan} — \textquotedblleft{}I recently read a lovely book.\textquotedblright{}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for hot, then the Arabic for crowded, then say \emph{ḥadīthan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ذات} \ar{مرة} (dhāta marra)}{ذات مرة (dhāta marra)}]{\ar{ذات} \ar{مرة} (dhāta marra) — once, one time}

\label{lesson:AR-C156-dhata-marra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for already; indeed, then the Arabic for last.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ذات} \ar{مرة}}
\textbf{\ar{ذات} \ar{مرة}} — \emph{dhāta marra} — \textquotedblleft{}once, one time\textquotedblright{}. It opens a story: \textbf{\ar{ذات} \ar{مرة} \ar{كانت} \ar{هنا} \ar{بحيرة}} — \emph{dhāta marra kānat hunā buḥayra} — \textquotedblleft{}Once there was a lake here.\textquotedblright{} \textbf{\ar{كانت}} is the past of \emph{to be}.
